title: Desk food truck: the build plan
intro: The plan for the battery-powered desk food truck, with 19 diagrams. Each section has its own Approve / Change and a note box: say anything you want different, in any section. The last block has five short questions; your answers decide which parts to order and unblock the software.

blocks.title: Five questions that decide what to order

questions.q: Which way do you want to build the electronics?
questions.detail: Section 5 compares them. The screen and battery are the same in all three, so changing your mind later costs about $10.

options.label: B: a little soldering (recommended)
options.text: Solder two rows of header pins: the classic first job. Proven low sleep current.

options.label: A: plug together
options.text: No soldering. Cheapest. Battery life is unproven until measured.

options.label: C: solder everything
options.text: Smallest and neatest. Fine soldering on small pads; better as a second build.

questions.detail: Section 3 draws both on the truck. The plan's dimensions assume 7.3 inch; the 4 inch would get its own set.

options.label: 7.3 inch (recommended)
options.text: Fills the side, reads from across a desk, shows up to four trucks.

options.label: 4 inch
options.text: In scale with a real serving window, room for detail round it, smaller text.

questions.q: How tall should the truck be?
questions.detail: The 7.3 inch screen's glass is 111 mm tall. 152 mm fits with only about 1 mm to spare above and below it; 155 mm gives room for a rim and for error.

questions.q: May I create a GitHub repo for this project, to run the morning job and host the page for free?
questions.detail: Free hosting needs the page to be public: anyone with the address could see today's trucks. Nothing secret goes in the repo; the Wi-Fi password lives only on the truck.

options.label: Not yet: build the software locally first
